description: Negative fixture (Python): bare calls whose callee is a parameter of an enclosing function or an outer closure scope must not resolve to the same-named module-level function. `run_with(cb)` calls its parameter `cb`, and `outer(run)`'s nested `inner` (QN `app.inner`) calls the closed-over parameter `run`; module-level `cb` exists precisely so a short-name resolver would fabricate the edge. Positive controls: `main` calls `run_with`, `outer`, and `helper`. (Nested definitions flatten to `<module>.<name>`; the closure control `inner -> run` is forbidden, not expected.)

forbidden_emitted_calls.reason: `cb` is run_with's parameter; the module-level `cb` is a different symbol. Any CALLS edge from run_with to *.cb is a phantom.
`run` is a parameter of the enclosing `outer`; a closure over a parameter is still parameter-bound.
